title: Mass Communications Systems Engineer (Mass Comm Sys Eng)
raw_text:
10-46T. Mass Communications Systems Engineer (Mass Comm Sys Eng) (Effective
202610)
CMF 46 (Army Civilian Acquired Skills Program (ACASP) designated MOS)
a. Major duties. Installs, operates, maintains, and performs unit and higher levels of maintenance
on mass communications equipment and systems in support of Army, Joint, and multinational
operations; maintains forms, records, prescribed load lists (PLL) special tools. and test
equipment; performs preventive maintenance checks and services (PMCS) on assigned vehicles
and generators. Duties for MOS 46T at each skill level are:
           (1) MOSC 46T1O. Operates and performs unit and higher levels of maintenance on
visual acquisition systems and cameras; studio accessories consisting of computer controlled
video switchers and audio mixers/consoles, synchronous generators, distribution equipment, and
amplifying equipment; motion/still photo imaging equipment; closed circuit systems; visual
imagery satellite, microwave, RF transmission and cable distribution systems associated with
visual information (VI) operations; operates and performs PMCS on assigned vehicles and power
generators.
           (2) MOSC 46T2O. Provides technical guidance on complex operations and
maintenance tasks; adjusts and maintains mass communications to prescribed standards;
ensures that proper techniques and procedures to diagnose malfunctions of VI and associated
equipment are employed; supervises receipt, storage, and issue of VI supplies.
           (3) MOSC 46T3O. Prepares work schedules and assigns tasks based on requirements;
plans technical aspects to satisfy on-air maintenance requirements; develops and advises
commanders on mass communications and VI production engineering requirements; establishes
and applies quality control measures in mass communications and VI productions; serves as
team leader on mass communications equipment repair teams.
           b. Physical demands rating and qualifications for initial award of MOS. The mass
communications systems engineer must possess the following qualifications:
           (1) A physical demands rating of Moderate.
           (2) A physical profile of 212221.
           (3) Normal color vision.
           (4) Qualifying scores.
               (a) A minimum score of 93 in aptitude area EL, 91 in aptitude areas ST and 97 in
aptitude area GT, effective 9 October 2023.
               (b) A minimum OPAT score of Long Jump (LJ) of140 cm, Seated Power Throw (PT)
of 400 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) of 140 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) of 40 shuttles in
Physical Demand Category of Significant.
           (5) High school graduate or equivalent.
           (6) Successful completion of one year of high school algebra and general science.
           (7) Mandatory formal training (completion of MOS 46T Course approved by the
Director, Army Public Affairs Center (APAC)) or meet the ACASP criteria per paragraph 9-
5b(5)(b) of this pamphlet and a Certificate of Completion (minimum course length 1 year)
associate degree in television Equipment Repair from vocational or technical school. Have 2
years of experience or a combination of formal training and experience totaling 2 years in
video/audio systems installation, video/audio equipment repair and use of test equipment.
Exception to policy (ETP) waiver may be granted by Director, APAC.
           (8) A security eligibility of SECRET.
                  (a) Requirement for a SECRET security eligibility is effective 1 October 2007 for
all new accessions into MOS 46T. Soldiers in the Delayed Entry Program (DEP) on or before 5
August 2007 with contracts for entry after 1 October 2007 are excluded from this requirement and
will be processed as in-service personnel per paragraph 8(b) below.
                  (b) Requirement for a SECRET security eligibility is effective 1 October 2010 for
all Soldiers holding MOS 46T who entered service prior to 1 October 2007 or were in the DEP per
paragraph 8(a) above.
           (9) A U.S. citizen.
                  (a) Requirement to be a U.S. citizen is effective 1 October 2007 for all new
accessions into MOS 46T. Soldiers in the Delayed Entry Program (DEP) on or before 5 August
 2007 with contracts for entry after 1 October 2007 are excluded from this requirement and will be
processed as in-service personnel per paragraph 9(b) below.
                  (b) Requirement to be a U.S. citizen is effective 1 October 2010 for all Soldiers
holding MOS 46T who entered service prior to
1 October 2007 or were in the DEP per paragraph 9(a) above.
           (10) Requests for exceptions to policy for training or reclassification must be submitted
to below email or address for final approval:
                  (a) Email: usarmy.meade.hqda-ocpa.mbx.apac-force-development@army
.mil.
                  (b) Mail: Director, Army Public Affairs Center, ATTN: Enlisted Personnel
Development, 4550 Parade Field Lane, Fort George G. Meade, MD 20755-5650.
      c. Additional skill identifiers. (Refer to table 12-8 for list of universal ASI’s associated with this
MOS.)
      d. Physical requirements and standards of grade. Physical requirements and SG relating to
each skill level are listed in the following tables:
           (1) Table 10-46T-1. Physical requirements.
           (2) Table 10-46T-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
           (3) Table 10-46T-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
